description: Four MCQs sampled from a pool of twelve; all four must be right. On failure show which were wrong, never the correct answer, and resample on retry so a reload isn't a free coin flip

data.question: What opens the per-PSP circuit breaker in the payouts platform?
choices: Five consecutive failures, or a >20% error rate over 60 seconds
A manual toggle in the ops console
data.rationale: agoda-payouts.md, 'Circuit breakers'. The thresholds are stated exactly.

data.question: Why did the original breaker miss the PSP-B incident?
choices: PSP-B degraded on latency without raising errors
The incident happened during a deploy freeze
data.rationale: p99 went 210ms → 9s with no error-rate signal. This is opinion #1 in kb.md, demonstrated.

data.question: What is the payout idempotency key derived from?
choices: (payout_id, attempt_number), generated and persisted before the call
A hash of the card token
data.rationale: Must be deterministic and must survive process death — that's the whole point of persisting it first.

data.question: How many mismatch classes does the nightly reconciliation produce?
Which reconciliation mismatch class pages a human immediately?
data.rationale: Duplicate issuance means real money left twice. ORPHAN_AUTH is manual but does not page.

data.question: What isolation level do the payout queue workers run at?
data.rationale: READ COMMITTED with SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.

data.question: Why was SERIALIZABLE rejected for the queue?
choices: Postgres doesn't support it at this volume
Serialization failures became a retry storm, and the correctness it bought was already explicit in the idempotency key plus advisory lock
data.rationale: He calls this the most arguable decision in the system and defends it without claiming it's obvious.

data.question: What happens to a payable when all three PSP breakers are open?
choices: The payout fails and the supplier is notified
It parks in a deferred state and a retry sweep picks it up
It falls back to bank transfer
It routes to a fourth PSP
data.rationale: And he says he'd model deferred explicitly from day one next time — an operational problem should not surface as a data problem.

data.question: Roughly what share of reconciliation mismatches auto-resolve?
data.rationale: The remaining ~6% lands in an ops queue with a class and a suggested action.

data.question: What is his actual relationship to NodusArt?
choices: Unpaid advisor — no commits, no equity, no on-call
data.rationale: The KB is deliberate about not upgrading this into 'Web3 engineer'.

data.question: What did he advise NodusArt to put on-chain?
choices: A content hash of the record plus a timestamp
Nothing — he argued against using a chain at all
data.rationale: Two orders of magnitude cheaper, and makes the record editable-with-history rather than immutable-and-wrong.

data.question: How does he describe his machine learning background?
choices: Undergraduate level and roughly seven years stale
data.rationale: Stated as a known gap. A candidate brief that claims otherwise has failed the no-invention rule.
